open_points.subject: BINARY_MAX_READ_BYTES configuration lifecycle
open_points.text: State 4 says “a missing, malformed or inconsistent [environment variable] … stops the start before any request is served,” while the changed State 3 text says “binary_storage reads BINARY_STORAGE_ROOT and BINARY_MAX_READ_BYTES at each binary read, each refusing that call when its value is missing or unusable.”
open_points.question: Does a missing or malformed BINARY_MAX_READ_BYTES prevent startup, or may the service start and refuse only later binary reads?
options: Startup fails because BINARY_MAX_READ_BYTES is a required startup setting.
Startup succeeds; each binary read loads and validates BINARY_MAX_READ_BYTES independently.
Startup validates an initial value, but later reads may observe and reject a changed value.
open_points.default_guess: Treat BINARY_MAX_READ_BYTES as a per-read exception and allow startup without it.

witness.initial: The database and other startup settings are valid, but BINARY_MAX_READ_BYTES is absent.
events: The deployment process starts the service.
A monitor requests liveness or readiness.
Later, an authorized staff member requests a protected binary.
outcomes: Runtime settings reject startup, so no health or binary route is served.
The service starts and health succeeds; only the later binary request is refused by binary_storage.
witness.observer: The deployment monitor and the authorized staff caller

open_points.subject: binary read failure caused by missing or unusable dynamic configuration
open_points.text: The changed text says binary_storage refuses a read when BINARY_STORAGE_ROOT or BINARY_MAX_READ_BYTES is “missing or unusable,” but the binary flows classify document concealment only for “missing object, oversize or unlisted media type,” while the general error policy maps storage failures to 500.
open_points.question: What HTTP outcome is produced when an otherwise authorized expense-document read fails specifically because a per-read binary environment value is missing or unusable?
options: Concealed not-found response (404), like the listed document delivery failures.
Storage/configuration failure (500), under the general storage-failure mapping.
A distinct declared configuration failure and mapping.
open_points.default_guess: Map it to the document endpoint’s concealed 404 because the failure occurs behind the authorized binary boundary.

witness.initial: A visible ExpenseDocument exists and its file_ref identifies readable PDF bytes; the staff caller is authorized, but BINARY_STORAGE_ROOT is removed or becomes unusable after startup.
events: The staff member requests the document.
expense_management authorizes the record and calls binary_storage.read_binary.
binary_storage reloads the environment and refuses the call.
outcomes: expense_management conceals the binary failure and the route returns 404.
The failure is treated as a storage/configuration outage and the route returns 500.

open_points.subject: dynamic binary read bound versus startup response ceiling
open_points.text: A14 says “The storage read bound is checked to be no larger than the declared response ceiling at start,” while the changed State 3 text makes binary_storage read BINARY_MAX_READ_BYTES anew “at each binary read.”
open_points.question: If BINARY_MAX_READ_BYTES changes after startup, who checks the newly read value against the declared response ceiling, and is a value above that ceiling unusable?
options: binary_storage rechecks every newly read value against the startup response ceiling.
The startup relationship is checked only once; later positive values are accepted even above that ceiling.
The effective read limit remains the startup value, despite rereading the environment.
open_points.default_guess: Have binary_storage reject a per-read value that exceeds the declared response ceiling.

witness.initial: The service starts with a 2 MB response ceiling and BINARY_MAX_READ_BYTES=1 MB.
events: An operator changes BINARY_MAX_READ_BYTES to 10 MB without restarting the service.
An authorized caller requests a valid 5 MB photo.
binary_storage reads the new value for that call.
outcomes: The new value is accepted and the 5 MB payload is returned.
The new value is unusable because it exceeds the response ceiling, so the photo request fails with storage unavailable.
